hcbs.title: HCBS vulnerability index
hcbs.label: Home & Community-Based Services
hcbs.analytical_question: HCBS is an optional Medicaid benefit with no federal floor. As the reconciliation law squeezes state financing, which states' HCBS programs are most at risk, and what would cuts mean for people who rely on home care to remain in the community?
hcbs.method: A composite 0-10 vulnerability index combining: (1) HCBS share of total Medicaid spending (stakes); (2) reliance on the now-capped provider-tax financing (exposure); (3) projected per-enrollee federal cut; (4) nonfederal share strain. Each component normalized 0-1 before weighting. Tier thresholds: High ≥6.5, Medium ≥4.0, Low <4.0. This is a risk screen, not a forecast of cuts.
hcbs.data_source: CMS-64 T-19 HCBS expenditure data (CMS Medicaid Financial Management Data); CMS HCBS waiver enrollment (1915(c) and 1115); KFF HCBS spending and enrollment tables.

managed_care.title: Managed-care MCO-tax exposure
managed_care.label: Managed Care
managed_care.analytical_question: More than two-thirds of Medicaid enrollees are in managed care plans. How do the reconciliation law's financing changes interact with managed care contracts, MCO taxes, and capitation rates, and what does that mean for plan participation and enrollee access?
managed_care.method: Analysis will combine: (1) MCO tax exposure: states with MCO provider taxes above 3.5% face the same hold-harmless cap as hospital taxes; (2) managed care penetration rate by state; (3) capitation rate adequacy: whether per-member per-month payments remain viable after the financing change. Source: CMS managed care enrollment report + state contract actuarial filings.
managed_care.data_source: CMS Medicaid Managed Care Enrollment Report (annual, CMS.gov); State Medicaid managed care contract rates (state-level, requires manual collection).

dual_eligibles.title: Dual-eligible spending concentration
dual_eligibles.label: Dual Eligibles
dual_eligibles.analytical_question: Dual eligibles (people enrolled in both Medicare and Medicaid) are a small share of Medicaid enrollment but account for 40-50% of spending in many states. Where is that concentration sharpest, and what do Medicaid financing cuts mean for people at the Medicare-Medicaid seam?
dual_eligibles.method: Dual enrollment share = duals ÷ total enrollment. Spending share estimated by applying a 3× per-capita cost multiple (a documented published approximation reflecting duals' LTSS, HCBS, and complex-care utilization). Concentration ratio = spending share ÷ enrollment share. States above the 1:1 line in a scatter of enrollment vs. spending share carry disproportionate fiscal exposure when Medicaid is cut.
dual_eligibles.data_source: CMS Medicaid managed care enrollment data (duals component); KFF, 'Medicaid's Role for Dual Eligible Beneficiaries' (2024); MedPAC and KFF for the 3× cost multiple.

data_sources.name: CMS-64 Medicaid Financial Management Data
data_sources.method: REST API via data.medicaid.gov: "Medicaid CMS-64 New Adult Group Expenditures" dataset (ID 00505e90-f8ac-5921-b12f-5e23ba7ffcf3). Four quarters are summed to produce annual federal fiscal year totals. No API key required.
data_sources.description: Authoritative quarterly state-level Medicaid expenditure data including total computable amount and federal share, summed to the most recent complete federal fiscal year.

data_sources.name: CMS Medicaid Beneficiary Enrollment Data
data_sources.method:
REST API via data.medicaid.gov: three datasets combined: (1) "Program Information for Medicaid and CHIP Beneficiaries by Year"
    (ID 5c267647-50e9-4a81-b2f2-8f23cec6631a) for total enrollment;
(2) "Major Eligibility Group Information by Year"
    (ID bffd757a-3ae9-42fc-809a-820c2919496b) for expansion adults;
(3) "Dual Status Information by Year"
    (ID 93b36a8e-4dd5-4ff4-9a8b-8c6537684705) for dual eligibles.
No API key required.
data_sources.description: State-level Medicaid enrollment by program type, eligibility group, and dual status: sourced from CMS MBES/T-MSIS data via data.medicaid.gov.

data_sources.name: KFF State Health Facts: Provider Taxes by Class
data_sources.method: Download the CSV export from the KFF State Health Facts provider taxes indicator page. The table includes per-state provider tax rates by provider class (hospital, nursing facility, MCO, etc.).
data_sources.description: Per-state provider tax rates broken out by provider class. The primary source for cap-exposure analysis, because it distinguishes exempt (nursing facility, ICF/IID) from subject (hospital, MCO, ambulance) classes: a distinction the analysis requires.

data_sources.name: KFF CBO State-Level Allocation Estimates
data_sources.method: Download the appendix table (CSV or Excel) from the KFF brief "Allocating CBO's Estimates of Federal Medicaid Spending Reductions Across the States." This gives per-state CBO allocations for the $226B provider-tax provision.
data_sources.description: KFF's per-state allocation of CBO's $226B provider-tax estimate. Used exclusively for validation: if the workbench exposure ranking agrees with the KFF/CBO allocation ranking, that is a cross-check pass.

data_sources.name: State Provider-Tax Scraper (Phase 2)
data_sources.method: Python scrapers under src/mfw/sources/state_scrapers/ fetch each state's provider-tax rate from primary sources (state statutes, agency pages). Run with: python -m mfw.sources.state_scrapers.run Writes data/current/state_provider_taxes.csv and a run log. Only sources classified "verified" in config/state_tax_sources.yaml have full adapters; "likely" sources produce stubs with confidence=likely. States where the structure is not_comparable (unit-based, capped, amount-targeted) carry effective_rate_pct=null, never fabricated.
data_sources.description: Per-state provider-tax rates scraped from 19 verified/likely primary sources. Non-percentage structures (unit_based, capped, amount_targeted) are reported in native units as not_comparable. Waiver states (RI, NV) are flagged separately from standard phase-down exposure states.

data_sources.name: CMS Medicaid Managed Care Enrollment Report
data_sources.method: Download the state-level enrollment Excel table from the CMS Medicaid managed care enrollment report (published annually by CMS).
data_sources.description: State-level Medicaid managed care enrollment by plan type. Needed for the Managed Care tab analysis (in progress).

provider_tax_ranking.description: Compares this workbench's state exposure ranking to KFF's published per-state CBO allocation of the $226B provider-tax estimate.
provider_tax_ranking.source: KFF, 'Allocating CBO's Estimates of Federal Medicaid Spending Reductions Across the States' (2025–2026). URL: https://www.kff.org/medicaid/issue-brief/allocating-cbos-estimates-of-federal-medicaid-spending-reductions-across-the-states/
